source_updates.title: Off-manifold robustness in synthesizer inversion with joint distribution flow matching
findings: synth inversion from real audio is an ambiguous projection onto the synthesizer manifold rather than unique parameter recovery
JDF improves several off-manifold metrics over an encoder-conditioned baseline but worsens Surge SOT from 0.232 to 0.317
JDF-A with unpaired real audio is almost tied with JDF without it on Surge off-manifold MSS 7.69 versus 7.68
the conditional baseline also differs architecturally, limiting causal attribution to the training objective
conditioning noise and CFG responses are model and domain dependent
the study uses isolated three-second one-shots and no human evaluation
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Treat output as a plausible synth-manifold projection; separate objective, architecture and unpaired-data effects and require multi-metric plus loudness-matched listening validation.

source_updates.title: On a Separate Note: Robust Score-Informed Note Separation with a Two-Stream TFC-TDF U-Net and Adaptive Set Ownership
findings: NoteSep requires aligned pitch onset and offset for every queried note and is not autonomous transcription
Adaptive Set Ownership reallocates mixture energy among concurrent independent note estimates
SCNS-Eval median SI-SDR is 7.39 dB versus 2.49 dB for score-informed NMF
Melodyne is not directly comparable because it receives no score and matched only 54.42 percent of scored notes
the signal contract is 16 kHz mono and the editing test uses stored note estimates rather than subtraction from the input
real transfer is limited to four PHENICX-Anechoic pieces and ten Bach10 quartets with no listening test
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use only with a trustworthy aligned score and audit independent-note sum consistency, octave leakage and preservation before local pre-mix editing.

source_updates.title: Do Audio Representations Compose Additively?
findings: CLAP beats permuted and label-overlap baselines on larger FSD50K combination holdouts while speech models do not consistently do so
all representations retain non-additive residuals
the diagnostic uses clip-level unordered semantic source labels
the study does not cover level pan dynamics phase temporal arrangement stems or mix quality
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use CLAP source-vector arithmetic only as a secondary diagnostic and retain waveform conservation, calibrated signal metrics and listening checks.

knowledge_cards: Real-audio synth inversion returns a plausible projection onto the synthesizer manifold, not uniquely recovered ground truth.
In synth-JDF, joint-density training explains most of the reported gain; the added unpaired-real marginal is nearly tied with JDF alone.
Improved MSS, wMFCC and RMS can coexist with worse SOT; one aggregate metric cannot certify timbral match.
Conditioning noise near tau 0.1 is a paper-specific sweep result, not a reusable setting.
CFG can help or hurt under domain shift and must be swept per model and task.
One-shot inversion does not validate full-song reference matching, effect automation or mix control.
NoteSep requires aligned pitch, onset and offset for every note and is not autonomous transcription or correction.
Independently estimated notes can violate mixture consistency; joint ownership can reduce but not eliminate that risk.
A 16-kHz mono separation result does not validate full-band stereo rock editing.
Synthetic stored-estimate editing metrics are not listener evidence for transparent in-mix edits.
CLAP embeddings are partially, not perfectly, additive across semantic source labels.
Embedding additivity does not imply waveform additivity or invariance to reverb, masking, time, level, pan or dynamics.
